title: Beazley Security Q3 report: exploited vulnerabilities start 28% of ransomware cases
geo_basis: global report; pin is a placeholder for the United States
summary: Insurance Business and Reinsurance News report that Beazley Security's Q3 threat report says ransomware cases starting with an exploited vulnerability rose from 14% in Q2 to 28% in Q3. Reinsurance News adds that reported ransomware incidents increased 38% on the previous quarter. Beazley's CEO advises starting with known exploited vulnerabilities and internet-facing applications.
plain: Beazley Security says more ransomware attacks now begin with an exploited software flaw: 28% in Q3, up from 14% in Q2, as reported by two trade publications.
exec: Beazley's data, as reported, shows exploited vulnerabilities starting 28% of ransomware cases, up from 14% in Q2.
action: Start with known exploited vulnerabilities and internet-facing applications, as Beazley Security's CEO advises, then prioritize systems that give access to credentials, cloud infrastructure or critical business operations.

sources.name: Insurance Business: Cyberattack tactics are outpacing what renewal forms ask
Reinsurance News: Ransomware incidents rise 38% in Q3'26 as attackers exploit vulnerabilities: Beazley Security

date_note: Dated by the trade articles' publication day; the Beazley report itself was not read.

validation.note: Insurance Business and Reinsurance News (independent publishers) each state the 14% to 28% figure; Beazley's own report not read.

review.note: Title, date, 14% to 28%, 38% and CEO advice checked against Insurance Business and Reinsurance News
